title: FirstQFM Foundation Model Cuts Quantum Gate Times by 33% on QuantWare QPU via NVIDIA Computing - Quantum Computing Report
gist: FirstQFM reported hardware-validated results where its quantum foundation model cut single-qubit gate times 33% on QuantWare's 21-qubit Contralto-D21 QPU at IQCC with no fidelity loss, and improved Bell-state fidelity on five qubit pairs, using NVIDIA compute and Quantum Machines control.

insights.claim: FirstQFM's quantum foundation model produced a 33% reduction in single-qubit gate execution time on QuantWare's 21-qubit Contralto-D21 QPU without degrading gate fidelity, validated by randomized benchmarking at the Israeli Quantum Computing Center.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Faster gates at equal fidelity is a direct, hardware-validated gain from AI-driven calibration.

insights.claim: The model generates zero-shot pulse-level gate optimizations from existing calibration data without requiring additional QPU runtime, integrating with Quantum Machines' OPX hardware and QUA calibration stack.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: No added QPU time lowers the cost of adoption for hardware operators.

insights.claim: The model also found pulse modifications that improved two-qubit Bell-state fidelities across five qubit pairs, addressing cross-talk and drift as QuantWare scales toward larger VIO-based QPUs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem

insights.claim: The foundation model was developed on NVIDIA's Leonardo supercomputer and open-source CUDA-Q platform before fine-tuning for QuantWare hardware, expanding CUDA-Q deployment across European quantum hubs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVIDIA's software stack keeps extending into quantum workflows.
